data.title: Harden advance.lock adoption against pid reuse: per-fire nonce in lock file + ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT marker

data.body: From AS-15 QA review (qa-priya). Current adoption rule: lock.source=='watcher' AND lock.pid == ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT pid. Residual spoof window: a shell carrying a stale ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT whose pid is reused by a NEW live watcher holding a fresh lock would let a manual tick wrongly adopt it and defeat single-flight. Odds are astronomical and the lock is etiquette-not-load-bearing (see advance-watcher.mjs header), hence backlog not blocker. Fix shape: watcher writes a random per-fire nonce into both the lock JSON and the marker (e.g. ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT=watcher:<pid>:<nonce>); step 0 matches pid AND nonce. Touches tickChildEnv + pin test + fire() lock write + advance.md step 0.

Plan written (cto-owen). Design: fireNonce() = randomBytes(8).hex (16 hex chars, node:crypto, zero new deps), generated once per fire; same value lands in the lock body ({pid,startedAt,source,nonce} via acquireLock(nonce)) and both marker transports (argv '/advance watcher:<pid>:<nonce>' as contract, ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT as belt). Step 0 adoption = source AND pid AND nonce all match; strict full-match back-compat (nonce-less lock never adopted — single machine, atomic upgrade, no rolling window; pre-upgrade leftovers fall to the unchanged staleness path). Staleness/release/verify stay nonce-blind by design. Pin tests updated in place, not duplicated: tickChildEnv 5-var key set UNCHANGED, values gain nonce; tickArgv argv[1] + signature order (pid, nonce, mode, rules); makeLockOps clean-acquire asserts written.nonce. Merge-tick note: restart the launchd watcher after merge (old-format markers fail safe as no-op, never double-fire).

Implementation complete (developer-marcus), commit 02e091d on feat/AS-16-lock-nonce. Built per plan: fireNonce() export (randomBytes(8).toString('hex'), 16 lowercase hex); acquireLock(nonce) required param, lock body now {pid, startedAt, source:'watcher', nonce}; marker watcher:<pid>:<nonce> on BOTH transports — tickArgv(watcherPid, nonce, permissionMode, rules) argument (contract) and tickChildEnv(env, watcherPid, nonce) env belt — no default nonce; advance.md step 0 + argument-hint updated to strict source+pid+nonce full-match adoption, missing nonce on either side = foreign, no legacy grace; staleness/release/verify untouched (nonce-blind by design). Pins updated IN PLACE per plan (tickChildEnv key-set assertion unchanged; tickArgv/makeLockOps call sites gain the nonce arg); new tests: fireNonce format+uniqueness, nonce threading lock<->argv<->env. Suite 163/163 in-container (was 161 + 2 new). No deviations from plan. POST-MERGE OPS STEP for the merging tick: restart the launchd watcher after merge — the running process still emits old-format watcher:<pid> markers, which fail safe (tick no-ops against its own lock; next message retries) until restart. Note: docker compose test image needed a BuildKit rebuild (classic builder produced arm64 vs the pinned linux/amd64); no repo change required.

QA review (qa-priya), cold, branch feat/AS-16-lock-nonce vs master. VERDICT: PASS — 5/5 acceptance criteria, zero inline fixes needed. (1) Lock body {pid,startedAt,source,nonce}, fireNonce()=randomBytes(8).hex, minted once per fire before acquisition — pinned by clean-acquire + format/uniqueness tests. (2) Both markers watcher:<pid>:<nonce> carry the fire's own nonce — threading test pins lock/argv/env agreement. (3) advance.md step 0 requires source+pid+nonce full match; missing nonce either side = foreign, no legacy grace; staleness wording byte-unchanged and explicitly nonce-blind. (4) Suite 163/163 in-container, run by QA (was 161 + the 2 planned new tests); all pins updated IN PLACE, tickChildEnv 5-var key set unchanged, no duplicated pins. (5) decide/isLockStale/releaseLock/verify untouched in diff; their tests changed call sites only. Scope guard: nothing outside advance-watcher.mjs / watcher.test.js / advance.md / .lattice state differs from master; no stray old-format marker references anywhere (grepped). FILER SATISFACTION: I filed this from my AS-15 review and replayed my own attack — stale marker with recycled pid vs new watcher's fresh lock: old marker's nonce predates the new lock's, match impossible short of 2^-64; missing nonce is explicit non-match; same-watcher/different-fire lingering markers also correctly rejected. Window closed, fail-safe in every branch (no-op, never double-fire). Strict no-legacy-grace is sound (one machine, atomic upgrade; pre-upgrade locks fall to the unchanged staleness path). 64-bit entropy is ample for this accidental-reuse threat. Nonce-on-argv visibility (ps) is a non-issue: the same value sits in the world-readable lock file, and the lock is etiquette-not-load-bearing — the nonce is an anti-accident token, not a credential. POST-MERGE OPS STEP for the merging tick: restart the launchd watcher after merge — until restart the running process emits old-format markers whose ticks correctly no-op (skipped tick, next message retries).
